- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if price is trending down.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to inflated 30d forecasts; apply dampening factor to post-spike days.
- Mean reversion is evident: if forecast is far above true outcome (e.g., >2.0) and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 15–30% in next 7–14 days.
- For 30d horizon, model frequently overpredicts mid-to-late period (days 15–30) — especially when sentiment is mixed or declining — apply downward correction to later days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/0.67 alternation, model tends to misalign with true price — adjust forecast to match sentiment cycle midpoint rather than extreme peaks.
